newsitem.title: USA: Norfolk Southern sees growth from Conrail deal.
newsitem.headline: Norfolk Southern sees growth from Conrail deal.

text.p: Norfolk Southern Corp. said Wednesday its proposed acquisition of more than half of Conrail Inc. will sharply boost revenues and earnings over the next several years.

Chief Financial Officer Henry Wolf said preliminary projections indicate the proposed transaction will increase revenues of the Norfolk, Va.-based railroad by more than 50 percent. Norfolk Southern posted a record $4.77 billion in transportation operating revenues in 1996.

"We will have, for the first time, the opportunity to develop a north-south market for both intermodal (rail-and- truck) and conventional traffic and reach fertile new markets as yet untapped," Wolf said in a conference call with Wall Street analysts.

Norfolk Southern and Richmond, Va.-based CSX Corp. late Tuesday released details of how they plan to divide Conrail's assets. A five-month battle for control of Conrail ended last month when the rival bidders agreed to buy Conrail together and split up its key routes.
The proposed $10.3 billion deal calls for Norfolk Southern to pay $5.9 billion for 58 percent of Conrail and CSX to pay $4.3 billion for 42 percent of the East Coast railroad.

Wolf said the proposed transaction will dilute per-share earnings by six percent in 1997 and 1998. It is then expected to boost earnings by five percent in 1999, 10 percent in 2000 and more than 15 percent in 2001 and beyond.

The transaction also is expected to result in significant cost savings for Norfolk Southern. The railroad anticipates $90 million of efficiencies in 1998, $220 million in 1999 and $350 million in 2000 and beyond.

Wolf also said the transaction will allow enable Norfolk Southern to become a major player in the east-west markets between the midwest and the northeast and leverage its Kansas City gateway to provide transcontinental service to the east.
Analysts were not permitted to ask questions during the conference call. Wolf said more details will be available when Norfolk Southern management meets with analysts in New York later this month.
CSX also planned to hold a similar type of conference call with analysts later Wednesday.
Shares of Norfolk Southern rose 75 cents to $87.625 in morning trade on the New York Stock Exchange.
